noProjects: No projects yet – create one under “Projects & apps”.
goTitle: What should your AI build today?
goText: Pick a project and an AI, describe the task – Hostwerk opens Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI in the project folder with your task already typed in.
goalPlaceholder: e.g. Build a contact form with spam protection
cmdPreview: This is what the terminal will show
goHint: The command then sits in the Hostwerk terminal – press Enter to start it.
goHintConnected: The AI reads your thought network by itself.
goHintConnect: Tip: connect under “Connect” and the AI knows your preferences.
typedInTerminal: It's in the terminal – press Enter to start
desktopLinux: For Windows and macOS – on Linux use Claude in the browser or in the terminal.
officialInstaller: Official installer – Hostwerk types it into the terminal.
noBrowser: No browser detected – here are all the ways.
desktopText: Claude Desktop reads your thought network by itself and adds new things – via the open MCP interface. Hostwerk adds itself to the Claude settings for that (with a backup). If Claude Desktop is running, it restarts briefly.
desktopOverwritten: Claude Desktop overwrote the Hostwerk entry (happens when Claude was running while connecting). Hostwerk adds it again once Claude is closed – or connect now.
otherToolsText: Every AI reads its own file in the project (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, Copilot, Cursor). Hostwerk writes your thought network into it as a marked section. Your own content stays, and a backup (.bak) is made first.
kgText: Code, docs and notes as a graph: a connected AI queries it instead of searching files and remembers insights. For claude.ai, ChatGPT or Gemini in the browser, copy the context into the chat or the project knowledge.
kgHint: The knowledge graph is its own extension – not installed yet? Settings → Extensions.
contextCopied: Context copied – now paste it into your AI’s web chat
deskNextStart: Connected – Hostwerk is included the next time Claude Desktop starts.
codeNotFoundText: Hooks and plugins need Claude Code – install it under “Get going”. Measuring and reading still work.
usageSub: Claude Code, last 14 days, local logs only
usageIntro: Shows tokens per day – so you see whether a saving tool or tip works. The first time, Hostwerk downloads the measuring program (ccusage, once).
noSessions: No Claude Code sessions found yet.
autoUpdateText: Check for new versions every 12 hours and update installed tools.
mcpCount: MCP servers registered in Claude Code
mcpCost: Each brings tool descriptions that cost tokens on every call.
noAutoWay: no automatic way for this system
runsInBackground: Running – you see the progress at the bottom right.
compareHint: The savings figures come from the projects themselves and depend a lot on how you work. Combining pays off: a hook for command output, short answers and the graph for large projects.
discoverSub: popular and maintained – not reviewed yet
discoverNone: Nothing new outside the catalog right now.
discoverHint: If a project proves itself, it goes into the catalog – then it's installable here with one click.
logEmpty: Nothing yet. As soon as a connected AI reads the thought network or adds something, it shows up here.
logNotConnected: Connect an AI under “Connect” first (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or another MCP app) – then you see here what it reads and remembers.
memText: What you told Hostwerk about yourself and your projects goes along with every AI in the AI assistant – not just Claude. Decide exactly what goes where.
memMindOff: The thought net is switched off in the settings – then nothing goes along.
memGraph: Matching excerpt from the knowledge graph (if the project has one)
memPrivate: Private notes never go along. Online providers additionally get secrets blacked out.
memWhoHint: New providers get the memory automatically – switch it off here.
memPreviewHint: Shows exactly the text the chosen AI gets from your memory.
memNothing: This AI gets nothing from the memory.
tplSaved: Template saved – everyone using this Hostwerk sees it
tplCopied: Templates copied – send them to your team and read them in with “Paste templates”
tplNothing: There are no templates in it.
loadFailed: Could not load the AI connection status
budgetUnknown: No usage measured today yet – tap “Measure” above.
budgetHint: From 80 % and when it is reached, Hostwerk tells you through your notifications.
Claude Code: daily token limit reached: Claude Code: daily token limit reached
Claude Code: 80 % of the daily token lim: Claude Code: 80 % of the daily token limit used
npmInstaller: Official npm package – Hostwerk types the command into the terminal (needs Node.js).
mcpCopied: Copied – paste it under MCP servers in the app
tokensClaudeOnly: Measuring, the daily limit and the token-saving tools on this page are for Claude Code. Usage of every AI in the AI assistant is under AI → Quotas.
tipsIntro: Tips marked “Claude Code” only apply there – Codex and Gemini CLI often have something similar (e.g. /compact or /compress). All others help with any AI.
clientsText: Pick the app you work with – Hostwerk shows you the right way. Then it reads your thought net and adds to it (through the open MCP interface).
otherClientText: Any app with MCP support (e.g. Zed, Cline, Jan, ChatGPT desktop with MCP) reads these settings. Paste them where the app lists its MCP servers – if the section is named differently, the “hostwerk” entry stays the same.
clientFileText: Paste the settings into {file} (in your user folder – create the file if it does not exist). If there is something in it already, only add the “hostwerk” entry. Then restart the app.
clientProjectFileText: Paste the settings into {file} in the project folder (create the file if it does not exist). If there is something in it already, only add the “hostwerk” entry.
cliOneText: Connects {name} with the thought net in all projects – through its official “mcp add” command. Hostwerk types it into the terminal, you confirm with Enter.
installFirst: {name} is not installed on this PC – install it first (guide).
